title: Spec rule artifact
description: One artifact per source work-unit. Holds the language-specification rules that this unit of the compiler implements. The deterministic chunker assigns `unit` and `source_hash`; the extraction model fills `rules`. Each rule carries a STABLE human-readable `id` (the addressing handle for the assembled spec).

unit.description: Deterministic work-unit id, e.g. 'sema/sema_expr/lower_binop'. Set by chunk.py; the model must echo it unchanged.

source.description: 'path#Lstart-Lend' the unit was sliced from. Echoed unchanged.

source_hash.description: Content hash of the unit's source bytes, supplied by chunk.py. The model writes it verbatim; chunk.py --plan compares it to the live source to decide staleness.

rules.description: The spec rules observable in this unit. Empty array is valid (plumbing-only units).

id.description: STABLE human-readable identifier: <domain>.<group>.<slug>, lowercase kebab segments. e.g. 'expr.cast.numeric-truncation', 'grammar.item.struct-decl', 'mono.subst.const-arg'. This is the permanent addressing handle — once assigned, NEVER change it (rename = breaking). Reuse the prior id given in the prompt for the same rule.

domain.description: Top-level spec domain; must equal the first segment of `id`.

title.description: Short human title for the rule (one line).

statement.description: The normative rule, stated precisely and implementation-agnostic (what the LANGUAGE does, not how this file does it). Prefer notation over paraphrase.

evidence.description: Source anchors that justify this rule: 'path#Lstart[-Lend]' references within this unit.

examples.description: Minimal Logos code snippets illustrating the rule (optional).

divergence.description: If this rule diverges from Rust, the DIVERGENCES.md tag (e.g. 'A1') or a one-line note. Omit if Rust-conformant.

uncertainty.description: Optional: note where the source is ambiguous and the rule is inferred rather than certain.

testability.description: How a conformance test confirms this rule (chunk.py coverage). 'behavioral' = a passing program asserts it; 'diagnostic' = a program must fail to compile with a specific message; 'transitive' = exercised via other tests, not directly testable (internal mono/codegen/layout invariants); 'untestable' = cannot be pinned by a Logos program. Absent ⇒ must be covered.
